Let $N = 4022$ and let $T$ be the number of draws until some value appears for the second time, counting that repeat draw. The first $k$ draws are all distinct with probability

$$Q_k = \prod_{i=0}^{k-1}\left(1-\frac{i}{N}\right) = \frac{N!}{(N-k)!\,N^k}.$$

Since $T > k$ exactly when the first $k$ draws are distinct, the tail-sum formula gives

$$E[T] = \sum_{k\ge 0} P(T>k) = \sum_{k\ge 0} Q_k = 1 + Q(N),$$

where $Q(N)$ is the Ramanujan Q-function, $Q(N) = \sum_{k\ge1} \frac{N!}{(N-k)!\,N^k}$.

The standard expansion is

$$Q(N) \approx \sqrt{\frac{\pi N}{2}} - \frac13 + \frac{1}{12}\sqrt{\frac{\pi}{2N}} + \cdots$$

So $E[T] \approx \sqrt{\pi N/2} + \tfrac23 + \tfrac{1}{12}\sqrt{\pi/(2N)}$.

- $\sqrt{6317.74} \approx 79.484$
- $\tfrac23 \approx 0.6667$
- correction $\approx 0.0016$

Check with $n=2$: the four paths give maxima 2, 1, 0, 0, so $E[M_2] = 3/4$. The formula gives $E|S_2| - P(S_2\ge 1) = 1 - 1/4 = 3/4$. ✓
